newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASX calls for Australia corporate law change.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASX calls for Australia corporate law change.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) called on Thursday for a review of Australia's Corporation Law because new technology has changed the ground rules for financial services industry regulation.

"Our current system of regulation pre-dates, for example, widespread use of the Internet," ASX managing director Richard Humphry said in the exchange's submission to the Wallis inquiry into Australia's finance sector.
"Regulators are struggling to keep pace with new products and other innovations made possible by technological change," Humphry said.
The Wallis inquiry, chaired by former Amcor Ltd chief Stan Wallis, is due to release a discussion paper in late November and make recommendations to the government in March.
Humphry said financial sector regulation must be sufficiently flexible to allow both regulators and market participants to respond to this rapid change.
"ASX's principal message to the inquiry was that Corporations Law was too long and too inflexible," Humphry said.
"A comprehensive re-write... would intoduce urgently needed flexibility so that market participants can respond speedily to market developments and new products," he said.
Humphry said the ASX favoured smaller not bigger regulatory agencies.
"Smaller organisations will, as a rule, be better equipped to respond quickly."

He said the ASX would be wary of any proposal for a mega-regulator overseeing the whole industry, instead favouring more formal status being given to the existing Council of Financial Supervisors to improve information sharing and eliminate regulatory overlap amongst existing regulators.
The ASX would also urge the treasurer to take a higher profile as minister for financial markets, Humphry said.

"To assist the treasurer in his financial markets role, the ASX supports the establishment of a new industry advisory body, the financial markets council, to facilitate regular, high level communication," Humphry said.
"The new Council would comprise representatives of the ASX, the Sydney Futures Exchange, the Australian Financial Markets Association and other key market participants," he said.
